newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Thursday with rising and active domestic A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen sucking money out of the repo markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.50 percent from 10.59 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose to 11.50 million lots from 7.73 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"A share market surges today are the major reasons for the rates to go up today," said one traders. Shanghai's A index closed up 2.02 percent today and Shenzhen rose 8.58 percent.
Traders expect the rates to consolidate on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday after the Finance Ministry said yesterday it would issue 20 billion yuan worth of seven-year T-bonds.
The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 122.50 yuan from 123.30 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 5.26 million lots from 3.39 million.
Traders said investors were worried that the new issue would attract liquidity from existing papers, which were likely to continue to fall in the short term.
